steps.say: Whether a pancreatic cancer can be removed is decided by angles on the scan, not by size alone. Clean arteries with limited vein touching mean go, a little arterial hugging means maybe after chemotherapy, and a wrapped coeliac or superior mesenteric artery means never. Irregular vessel walls are counted as invasion even without full encasement.
steps.tx: **Borderline resectable** (tumour touching but not encasing vessels) means limited **arterial abutment** (tumour hugging the artery) under **180** degrees, or vein involvement over **180** degrees or lesser contact with irregular walls or clot, still allowing resection after chemotherapy, while clean arteries with vein contact of **180** degrees or less and smooth walls are resectable upfront. Encasement over **180** degrees of celiac or superior mesenteric artery is unresectable.

steps.say: The Whipple removes the head of the pancreas together with everything stuck to it, the duodenum, the end of the bile duct and the first loop of jejunum. Reconstruction follows the Child order of joins. When the disease is benign, the stomach outlet is spared to keep emptying normal, while tumours reaching the antrum or pylorus take it too.
steps.tx: **Pancreaticoduodenectomy** (Whipple: removing pancreatic head with duodenum, bile duct end and first jejunal loop) uses **Child reconstruction** (pancreas joined first, then bile duct, then stomach in sequence), and the pylorus-preserving variant suits benign and premalignant disease best. Classic antrectomy is chosen when tumour reaches the antrum or pylorus.

vis.alt: Double duct sign from pancreatic head mass with Whipple procedure diagram.
vis.caption: Double duct sign marks head tumours suited to pancreaticoduodenectomy. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Cancers of the body and tail are removed from left to right with the spleen, sweeping the fatty envelope behind the kidney. The posterior plane takes Gerota fascia with the specimen to clear the margin where these tumours love to linger. Nodes along the splenic and coeliac vessels come out with the specimen for staging. Adrenal or posterior involvement is the signal to switch to the posterior plane, taking the adrenal.
steps.tx: **RAMPS** (radical antegrade modular pancreatosplenectomy: dissecting left to right through body-tail tumours) with **N1** nodes for body-tail cancers secures posterior margin clearance. The posterior plane removes **Gerota fascia** (renal envelope behind the pancreas) with the adrenal, while anterior RAMPS fits tumours standing clear of the adrenal gland.

steps.say: Chemotherapy around surgery has transformed results, and six months of modified FOLFIRINOX after resection is now the standard for fit patients. Borderline tumours get the same drugs first, with falling CA 19-9 marking conversion to operability. Frail patients who cannot tolerate four drugs are given gemcitabine with capecitabine instead.
steps.tx: Modified **FOLFIRINOX** (four-drug combination) given for **6** months stands as the **adjuvant** (postoperative chemotherapy) benchmark after resection following PRODIGE 24, with preoperative FOLFIRINOX converting borderline disease as falling CA 19-9 marks operability. Gemcitabine-capecitabine fits patients too frail for four drugs.

steps.say: A leak of pancreatic juice is defined by numbers, not by looking at the drain. Amylase above three times the normal upper limit on or after the third day means a fistula, with harmless biochemical leaks separated from grades B and C that bring organ failure. Most settle with drainage and antibiotics, while persistent ones need image-guided drainage or reoperation.
steps.tx: Postoperative **pancreatic fistula** (leaking pancreatic juice) means **drain amylase** (drain fluid enzyme level) above **3** times the normal serum upper limit on or beyond day **3**; a transient biochemical leak is not a true fistula, while ISGPS grades B and C bring infection, bleeding or organ failure. Management is drainage and antibiotics, with somatostatin analogues only for high-risk glands. Persistent leaks need image-guided drainage, occasionally reoperation.

nodes.label: Amylase over 3 times serum from day 3

steps.say: A stomach that will not wake up after a Whipple is graded just like a leak. Needing the nose tube past day three, or having it put back, marks delayed emptying across grades A to C. Prokinetics coax it along while the join swelling settles. Reoperation for emptying alone is rare.
steps.tx: **Delayed gastric emptying** (stomach failing to wake after resection) with a nose tube still needed past day **3** or reinserted afterwards is graded ISGPS A to C across tube days 4 to beyond **14**, and managed with **prokinetics** (motility drugs) and nutrition support while swelling settles. Erythromycin bridging covers the interim weeks, and reoperation for emptying alone is rare.

steps.say: Every pancreatic cancer now gets its genes read, because the letters change the drugs. BRCA one, two and PALB faults predict platinum response, with olaparib maintenance afterwards for metastatic BRCA-mutated disease. KRAS, mismatch repair and NTRK testing of the tumour guides trials and targeted drugs, with immunotherapy reserved for mismatch-repair-deficient tumours. Positive inherited results send the whole family for counselling.
steps.tx: Germline **BRCA** testing (BRCA1, BRCA2 and PALB2 faults) guides platinum sensitivity, with **olaparib** (PARP inhibitor) maintenance per POLO for metastatic BRCA-mutated disease responding to platinum; all patients get somatic **KRAS** (common driver mutation), mismatch repair and NTRK profiling, with immunotherapy guided by mismatch repair status. Cascade testing follows positive germline results.

steps.say: When the tumour cannot be removed, the surgeon's job turns to keeping bile, food and comfort flowing. A metal stent through the blockage is open for six to ten months, far longer than plastic. Injecting alcohol around the coeliac nerves eases the gnawing back pain, while a blocked duodenum is stented or bypassed. Early palliative care runs alongside.
steps.tx: Inoperable head tumours receive endoscopic metal biliary stenting lasting **6 to 10** months plus **celiac plexus neurolysis** (nerve-block injection for back pain), while **duodenal stenting** (enteral metal stent) or gastrojejunostomy relieves outlet blockage. Early palliative care improves comfort and quality of life alongside cancer treatment.
